partial_case.facts: The resident reported in January 2023 that her kitchen window was cracked. She complained to the landlord on 9 August 2023 because it had not repaired the window during that time. The resident called the landlord to log a complaint that her kitchen window was cracked and the landlord had not repaired it. The landlord replied to the resident at stage 1 on 13 September 2023, acknowledging there was a delay in completing the repairs and apologising for the service failures. The landlord raised an appointment to address the issue and awarded £110 compensation for the inconvenience caused. The resident emailed the landlord requesting a review of her complaint. She sent further emails to the landlord who did not reply to her until 23 December 2023. The landlord escalated her complaint on 3 January 2024. The landlord responded to the resident at stage 2 on 31 January 2024, accepting there had been further delays in completing the window repair and acknowledging that the repair delay was excessive and there was also a failure in complaint handling. It awarded £235 compensation in total and provided a date for the repair to be completed. The resident told us she was unhappy with the handling of the repair and the level of compensation awarded.

key_reasoning_quotes.text: There were failures in the landlord's response to the resident's repair request which caused severe delays.
There was a delay by the landlord in responding to the resident's complaint at stage 1 and it failed to escalate the resident's complaint within its timescales.
The repair was completed over 14 months after the resident had initially reported the repair. As the landlord acknowledged, these delays were significant and had an adverse impact on the resident.
The compensation offered does not reflect the impact these failures had on the resident.
